briefing:
إليك التقرير التكتيكي الشامل للجولة رقم 9 الصادر عن محرك التحليل الإحصائي والقواعد الذهبية:

---

### 1. التكتيك المعتمد وموقف الترتيب (AGGRESSIVE Strategy)
بناءً على الترتيب الحالي (**10,618,666**)، لا مجال للتحفظ أو اللعب الدفاعي التقليدي؛ التكتيك المعتمد هو **الهجومي التعويضي (AGGRESSIVE)** القائم على مبدأ "نقاط اليوم قبل الغد". الموقف يتطلب التضحية باللاعبين المتراجعين وتفعيل خيار الخصم السلبي (-4 Hit) باحترافية، لاقتناص فارق النقاط (Upside) وتجاوز المنافسين في سلم الترتيب العام بسرعة وحسم.

---

### 2. مدى مطابقة القرارات للقواعد الذهبية (Gold Rules Compliance)
أظهرت القرارات التزاماً صارماً ومبرهناً بالقواعد التاريخية المستخرجة من المحرك:
*   **جدوى الخصم السلبي (-4 Hit):** تتوافق التضحية بـ 4 نقاط تماماً مع قاعدة المحرك التي تؤكد أن أخذ السالب يُعد مثالياً رياضياً للوصول إلى الانفجار المرجو (+10.8 نقطة صافي ربح فوري للتبديلات المثالية). دمج التبديلين يمنحنا قفزة في النقاط المتوقعة المباشرة من (3.0 xP) للاعبين المباعين إلى (10.6 xP) للقادمين، مما يغطي تكلفة التبديل (-4) ويحقق فارقاً إيجابياً فورياً.
*   **استراتيجية الكابتن:** اختيار **Tavernier** ككابتن يطابق القاعدة الذهبية المثبتة بثقة 80%، والتي تنص على أن الكباتن الأكثر كفاءة يبلغ متوسط سعرهم **£6.5m** (حيث يُختار الكباتن الأغلى من £9.5m في 20% فقط من الجولات المثالية).
*   **هيكلية خط الوسط والأسعار:** يمتلك الفريق خط وسط متفجراً (Palmer, Mbeumo, Tavernier, Barcola)، وهو ما يتماشى مع قاعدة تخصيص الميزانية التي تمنح الأولوية لوسط الملعب بنسبة 39.8% من الإنفاق الأساسي. كما أن التعاقد مع أغطية دفاعية بسعر أقل من £6.0m يطبق قاعدة كفاءة الأسعار (2.69 نقطة لكل مليون).

---

### 3. التحليل الرياضي والتكتيكي للتبديلات (-4 Hit)
*   🔴 **بيع Calafiori (xP: 2.5) ──► 🟢 شراء Konsa (xP: 5.9 | £4.7m):** التخلص من Calafiori قرار حتمي نظرًا لتراجع انتاجيته ومخاطر تدويره (Flop). الشراء يمنح الفريق استقرارًا دفاعيًا ومعدل نقاط متوقعة مرتفع جداً يتجاوز ضعف اللاعب المباع.
*   🔴 **بيع Thomas (xP: 0.5) ──► 🟢 شراء Bassey (xP: 4.7 | £4.5m):** بيع Thomas يعالج عبء اللاعبين غير المنتجين في التشكيلة، بينما Bassey يمثل خيار خياراً دفاعياً أساسياً بتكلفة ممتازة ومعدل xP تصاعدي.
*   **المحصلة على مدار 3 جولات:** التبديلات لا توفر فقط ربحاً فورياً متوقعاً في هذه الجولة، بل تضمن مساراً أسهل وتدوير خيارات أكثر مرونة وتؤمن خط الدفاع على المدى المتوسط، مما يبرر تكلفة الخصم السلبي (-4) بنجاح.

---

### 4. مبررات شارة القيادة (C) والنائب (VC)
*   **الكابتن (C): Tavernier (BOU) - xP: 7.8**
    تم التكبيت بناءً على أعلى سقف نقاط متوقع (xP) في الفريق لهذا الأسبوع، وتطبيقاً لقاعدة الكابتن الذهبية التي تفضل أصحاب السعر المتوسط الأكثر فاعلية مقارنة بالأسماء الرنانة المرهقة للميزانية.
*   **النائب (VC): Isak (LIV) - xP: 6.8**
    تم اختيار Isak كنائب قائد ليوفر غطاءً أمنياً متيناً بخيار هجومي ذي سقف عالٍ ومعدل استقرار مرتفع في حال حدوث أي مفاجآت غير متوقعة لمشارك Tavernier.

---

### 5. نصيحة استراتيجية الخواص وحماية ميزانية الفريق
*   **إدارة الخواص (Chips):** يمتلك الفريق ترسانة كاملة (Wildcard x2, Free Hit x1, Triple Captain x1, Bench Boost x1). التوصية الصارمة هي **الاحتفاظ بالخواص كاملة** واستغلالها حتمياً في الجولات المزدوجة (DGW) والبلانك (BGW) لضمان تحقيق أعلى عائد تراكمي للنقاط.
*   **إدارة السيولة:** الاحتفاظ برصيد ضخم في البنك قدره **£7.2m** يمنح الفريق مرونة تكتيكية فائقة للتحرك السريع في الجولات القادمة لضم أي نصر مستجد أو استعادة أسماء كبرى دون الحاجة لإجراء عمليات جراحية مكلفة في التشكيلة.

---

### الخلاصة التنفيذية
التشكيلة الحالية (3-4-3) بدخول Konsa و Bassey، مع منح شارة القيادة لـ Tavernier، تضع الفريق في أفضل موقع هيكلي ورياضي ممكن لاختراق الترتيب والقفز بقوة. التضحية بنقاط التبديل (-4) تم تعويضها حسابياً في خط الدفاع، وتوفر الميزانية (£7.2m) يمنحنا اليد العليا للجولات المقبلة. اعتمد التشكيل بثقة وانطلق نحو تقليص الفارق.

press_wire.title: Saturday night at Villa Park
press_wire.summary: Fixtures Aston Villa Vs. Fulham - Sat, Oct 31 2026, 20:00 Aston Villa look to return to winning ways on Saturday night, entertaining Fulham at Villa Park. The Villans return to Premier League action on Halloween after exiting the Carabao Cup at the hands of Bournemouth in midweek, having secured consecutive league wins against Newcastle United and Manchester City. Unai Emery’s men will hope to make it three league wins in a row in B6, while extending their unbeaten league streak to five matches. Fulham also bowed out of the League Cup on Wednesday night, falling 1-0 at home to Crystal Palace having secured their first two wins of the Premier League season – over newly-promoted Hull City and Coventry City – in their two prior outings. Álvaro Arbeloa’s side sit 15th in the league table after eight matches, though like Villa, are also going in search of a third successive league triumph. Stats Aston Villa have lost just one of their 18 home Premier League matches against Fulham (W12 D5), a 2-1 defeat in April 2014. Fulham won their last Premier League game against Aston Villa and have registered consecutive wins against them just once before in the competition, winning both games in 2013/14. Villa boss Unai Emery has won eight of his nine Premier League matches against Fulham (L1), a points-per-game of 2.67; of managers to take charge of 5+ games against the Cottagers, only Pep Guardiola (3, won 12/12) and Mauricio Pochettino (3, won 6/6) have a higher ratio. The Villans are looking to win three consecutive Premier League matches for the first time since a run of eight in November and December last season. Fulham won none of their first six Premier League games this season (D2 L4) but have won each of their last two, 1-0 wins over Hull and Coventry. The only two Premier League sides to start with six winless games then win three in a row are Newcastle in 2003/04 and Stoke in 2015/16. Villa have only won two of their last 12 Premier League matches in August and September (D5 L5), compared to eight wins in their last 10 games across October and November (D1 L1). Fulham are looking for three Premier League wins in a row for the first time since December 2025, while they last achieved that without conceding a goal back in April 2019. Nicolas Jackson has scored four goals in his last four Premier League appearances for Villa, as many as he’d managed in his previous 24 games in the competition (4 in 21 for Chelsea, 0 in 3 for Villa). Only Man City duo Erling Haaland (2.92) and Rayan Cherki (2.32) have outperformed their xG more than Jackson this season (2.02). Fulham’s average possession (58%), successful passes per game (505) and passing accuracy (86.7%) in the Premier League this season are all their best totals on record since 2003/04. Two of the four players with the most touches in the opposition box in the Premier League this season are Fulham’s Josh King (52, 1st) and Oscar Bobb (43, 4th). King is having 7.1 per 90 minutes, with only one Fulham player on record (since 2008/09, 500+ mins played) averaging more in a season – Bobby Zamora in 2010/11 (8.6). The Last Meeting Villa fell to defeat in the last meeting between they and the West London outfit in April. With 2025/26 drawing to a close, Unai Emery’s men travelled to Craven Cottage and went down 1-0, as Ryan Sessengnon fired home two minutes before the break to seal three points. The result didn’t stop the Villans from reaching their goals for the season, as they secured Champions League football less than a month later. Team News There could be more changes for Unai Emery’s men, after the Villa boss rotated in midweek for Carabao Cup action. Matteo Ruggeri and Aaron Wan-Bissaka remain sidelined with injury, while Amadou Onana is a long-term absentee. Fulham will be without Ryan Sessegnon, who serves the final game of his three-match suspension, meaning Antonee Robinson should continue at left-back. It remains to be seen whether or not David Affengruber and Emile Smith Rowe will feature, having both missed the Carabao Cup defeat to Palace. Managers' Pre-Match Thoughts “Tomorrow, Fulham, prioritising Premier League clearly, and this is the message, because to keep our consistency, to keep our demands and work every day to get these demands to keep, to get this commitment to keep our consistency like we did the last year, each match is a test.” - Unai Emery “For us, it's a new challenge to beat a team like Aston Villa, and that is important for us to prove that we can beat anyone. So, yes, I think we will go there and we will give our best, thinking we can beat any team.” - Álvaro Arbeloa

press_wire.title: WE NEED TO BE READY FOR A TOUGH GAME: TOM MALLINSON
press_wire.summary: Mallinson previews Subway Players Cup clash with Burnley Forest looking to build on positives from Newcastle Looking for more of the same in second meeting with the Clarets this season Tom Mallinson has said his side need to be ready for a tough game when Nottingham Forest face off against Burnley in the Subway Players Cup at the City Ground on Sunday; the second meeting between the sides at the World-Famous this season after last month's league meeting, in which the Reds came out on top. “Getting the home fans behind us is always a nice thing and they definitely had that opportunity at the weekend against Newcastle and 2,200 people was outstanding! It’s now for us to keep being exciting in what we do out on the pitch and how we prepare ourselves for that is to be ready for Burnley and if we do that and we can produce a really good performance, then we can definitely give the fans something to cheer about. We need to be ready for a tough game because Burnley won’t be happy to have lost the game to us in the league and in the cup we need to win a game and we haven’t been successful with that in the Villa game and the Sheffield United game. We want to make sure we’re more threatening in the final third. We had lots of chances against Burnley in the league. I think they will have definitely learnt from that game, as we have about how we can be better and I think that’s what we’ll take out for the rest of the week, it’s more what do we affect. We’re never too worried about what oppositions do, it’s about how we play and how we are, our style, both with and without the ball and how we conduct ourselves. That’s what our focus is and hopefully at the weekend we will put together a performance that gets us a win but that also puts a real stamp on about who we are as a team."

press_wire.title: Bournemouth tickets
press_wire.summary: Tickets for Fulham's fixture against AFC Bournemouth will go on sale next week! Join us in SW6 as we welcome The Cherries for Premier League action on Sunday 29th November, kick-off 2:05pm. Tickets for this fixture will go on sale to 2026/27 Members* from 9:30am on Tuesday 3rd November (one ticket per person). 2026/27 Season Ticket Holders will be able to purchase additional seats from 9:30am on Thursday 5th November (four tickets per person), before going on sale to Supporters with a Previous Booking History** from 9:30am on Monday 9th November (four tickets per person). Any remaining tickets will go on General Sale*** from 9:30am on Wednesday 11th November (four tickets per person). Tickets can be secured from Tuesday online at fulhamfc.com/tickets, from the Fulham FC Ticket Office in person (Mon-Fri, 9:30am-4:30pm) or by calling 0203 871 0810 (Mon-Fri, 9:30am-5pm). More information regarding on sale dates and pricing can be found here. BUY TICKETS FROM TUESDAY Important Information The 2026/27 season will see new Premier League requirements implemented for assigning tickets to supporters, with every seat sold being assigned to the individual who intends on attending the related match. Each attendee's name and contact details must be registered with the club. This means if a supporter purchases four tickets for a fixture, each ticket will need to be assigned to a unique client reference number. In the instance of a Season Ticket Holder purchasing additional tickets during their priority window, each ticket that they are purchasing will need to be assigned to each individual who intends on attending the related match. We therefore encourage all supporters planning on attending fixtures at Craven Cottage to keep their friends and family network updated to ensure they can easily assign tickets at the point of purchase. Supporters can follow our step-by-step guide on how to do this here. *2026/27 Membership must have been purchased prior to 5pm on Thursday 29th October in order to be eligible to purchase tickets during the Members' priority window. **To qualify for Booking History status, supporters must have purchased a Fulham FC Men's First Team match ticket since the 2021/22 Season. Booking History status is not valid if supporters have only previously purchased tickets against the same opposition, in this case AFC Bournemouth. You must have Booking History status prior to 5pm on Thursday 29th October in order to be eligible to purchase tickets during this window. ***Subject to postcode restrictions - Fulham FC will be monitoring bookings and any tickets purchased by supporters who live in the vicinity of Bournemouth (and local areas) who do not have a previous booking history with us, will be terminated.

press_wire.title: JAIR CUNHA NAMED IN BRAZIL SQUAD
press_wire.summary: Jair receives second Brazil call Defender named in November squad Brazil face Japan and Singapore in double-header Jair Cunha has received his second senior call-up to the Brazil squad. The Nottingham Forest defender received his first senior call-up before the last international period, making his senior international debut against Australia following an outstanding start to the Premier League season with the Reds. The defender earned three caps for Canarinho during the international period. Brazil travel to Japan and Singapore in November’s international period for two friendlies. Jair has made seven appearances in total for the Reds in 2026/27, taking his total to 22 in the Garibaldi in all competitions.

press_wire.title: FOREST PREVIEW | EVERYTHING YOU NEED TO KNOW ABOUT OUR TRIP TO BRENTFORD
press_wire.summary: Forest face Brentford Reds searching for third successive win in west London Both sides are on 16 wins against each other going into the clash Nottingham Forest head to Brentford in search of a third successive win at the Gtech Community Stadium on Saturday 31 October. The Reds have won each of our last two trips to the stadium 2-0; goals from Ola Aina and Anthony Elanga secured the win in 2024/25, while Igor Jesus and Taiwo Awoniyi were on the scoresheet last season in west London. Forest also claimed maximum points in the first meeting between the clubs last season with a 3-1 win at the City Ground in what was Keith Andrews’ first game in charge of the Bees. Last time out, the Reds went ahead on the road against Ipswich Town through Neco Williams, only for Julio Enciso to level before half-time, meaning the spoils were shared in Suffolk. Brentford, meanwhile, are without a win since mid-September, when the Bees emphatically saw off Chelsea on home soil 3-0. In total, the sides have met 43 times, with both clubs winning 16 of those games. The remaining 11 have ended all square. Our opponents After finishing Keith Andrews’ maiden campaign as Brentford’s head coach in ninth place in the Premier League, the Bees currently occupy sixth in the early-season table, having lost just one of their opening eight league matches. That loss came in their last home outing, when Liverpool claimed a 2-1 win, a result arguably influenced by Yehor Yarmolyuk’s sending-off on the stroke of half-time. The wins have come against Tottenham Hotspur and Chelsea on home soil, with both games ending 3-0 in the Bees’ favour. The remaining matches have all ended in draws. Brentford exited the Carabao Cup in midweek, losing 3-2 away at Sunderland despite a late fightback after finding themselves 3-0 down at the Stadium of Light. The key OPTA stats and facts Brentford were unbeaten in each of their first four Premier League games against Nottingham Forest (W2 D2) but have now lost three of their last four (W1). Nottingham Forest have won their last two league games against Brentford, only once registering three in a row, doing so in the Championship between February 2019 and January 2020. Nottingham Forest have lost their last five league matches played on Halloween, a run stretching back to the first Premier League season in 1992-93 when they lost 1-0 to Ipswich. Brentford are one of two teams (along with Man City) to have scored in all eight of their Premier League games so far this season. Their 1-1 draw with Hull last time out was the only time they’ve not scored first. Brentford have lost just one of their last nine Premier League home games (W3 D5), though it was their last one against Liverpool. They’ve not lost consecutive league matches at the Gtech Community Stadium since January/February 2025, the first of which was against Liverpool. Nottingham Forest have won just five of their last 23 Premier League games (D10 L8), the joint fewest of any ever-present side since the start of February, along with Tottenham. No side has scored fewer Premier League goals so far in 2026-27 than Nottingham Forest (6). Forest have an xG of 13.5 so far this term, giving them the biggest xG underperformance (-7.5). Nottingham Forest have scored 36 Premier League goals in 2026, with 28 of them coming away from home (78%). It’s the highest percentage of goals scored in away games by any top-flight team in a year, of sides who featured in the top division for the full calendar year. Brentford’s Jaidon Anthony has scored three goals in four Premier League appearances against Nottingham Forest, including in both home games against them for Bournemouth in 2022/23 and Burnley in 2025/26, both in 1-1 draws. Morgan Gibbs-White is one of three players with 20+ chances created in the Premier League this season (20), with no player creating more big chances than the Nottingham Forest captain (7). Team news Oliver Glasner says Dan Ndoye and Nicolás Domínguez are doubts for the trip to Brentford, as discussed in his pre-match press conference. However, the Reds are boosted by the return of Neco Williams, who trained all week after a heavy landing on his elbow against Ipswich. Brentford will be without Rico Henry and Fábio Carvalho at the Gtech Community Stadium while Yehor Yarmolyuk is suspended after being sent off against Liverpool. Kaye Furo is also likely to be on the sidelines while Antoni Milambo and Josh Dasilva are still recovering from injury. What they're saying “I’m expecting the toughest game we’ve had in the last seven to eight days. “They’ve played very well in games and have some magnificent players who can hurt you if given the opportunity. “If you look at the table, you would get a false sense of where they’re at with their performances. If they continue performing the way they are, they will be in a very different position.” Oliver Glasner's pre-match press conference Kit confirmations Our adidas away kit will make its second appearance of the season against the Bees, but with a slightly altered look. Our starting goalkeeper will wear the blue kit, as seen on Trentside this season. Brentford will sport their traditional red and white stripes, with accompanying black shorts and socks. Last five against Brentford 25/01/2026 – Brentford 0-2 Forest 17/08/2025 – Forest 3-1 Brentford 01/05/2025 – Forest 0-2 Brentford 21/12/2024 – Brentford 0-2 Forest 20/01/2024 – Brentford 3-2 Forest Previous meeting In the middle Darren England will officiate our trip to Brentford on Saturday 31 October. Scott Ledger and Mat Wilkes are the assistant referees. Farai Hallam is the fourth official, while Andrew Kitchen and Tom Nield are the VAR and assistant VAR, respectively.

press_wire.title: Emery looks ahead to Fulham encounter
press_wire.summary: Fixtures Aston Villa Vs. Fulham - Sat, Oct 31 2026, 20:00 Unai Emery met with the media on Friday afternoon, to look ahead to Aston Villa’s Premier League meeting with Fulham. The Villans take on the Cottagers at Villa Park on Saturday (ko 8pm), looking to secure a third successive league win. And the Villa boss sat down for his pre-match media briefing at Bodymoor Heath, discussing his side’s Halloween opponents, squad depth, Nicolas Jackson’s form and more. Here are the key lines from Friday’s press conference. On Fulham... “They are playing really well. They are competing fantastic (in) the last matches, even losing against Crystal Palace in the Carabao Cup. In the league, they are really fantastic. “Of course, (Álvaro) Arbeloa, he has experience in England. He played here, he has experience in football for a long time. He had very good coaches. “Now, how they are playing, is really like a coach with experience and a coach managing tactically a lot of things.” On Nicolas Jackson... “He’s showing us, and I knew him like that, being very, very professional, focusing football as a priority in his life. “He has this commitment with football himself, to try to get his responsibility as high as possible, to try to get his best with the team here, with Aston Villa. “I am happy, but as well, I know he has a lot of work to do as well, to try to get better, to try to be consistent. “He needed some adaptation at the beginning, but he’s still needing some adaptation to do with us, and keep going forward.” On squad depth and handling a busy period... “The only focus is tomorrow, the match tomorrow. But, of course, how we are doing our way at the beginning of the season, even in the pre-season, everything has a plan, and the plan is try to play focusing each match, each competition, with the players (who) are ready and available to play, with the objective to have as well, some players (who) need confidence, time, adapting us, time to get fit, time after some injuries. “So, how we are building the team is a process, and the process is going, but each match is the objective. “If I am thinking, if we are thinking, after the match tomorrow against Fulham, we are making a mistake, and we are wrong, completely wrong. “So, tomorrow, Fulham, prioritising Premier League clearly, and this is the message, because to keep our consistency, to keep our demands and work every day to get these demands to keep, to get this commitment to keep our consistency like we did the last year, each match is a test. “In Premier League, we are (in a) lack of points. Of course, we are progressing, we are getting better, but if we want to be consistent like the last year and (in) the top positions, we must focus tomorrow (on) the match, prioritising 100% and focusing, respecting them, preparing the game, playing so, so focused and intense the match requires, and respecting them.” On Leon Goretzka... “He started being available two weeks ago, and progressively playing minutes, understanding our tactical idea, adapting of us, and we are adapting as well to him, because his quality is clear. “His capacity to help us with his experience, we’ll see it, but we believe. He played in the starting 11 on Wednesday, one step forward for him to get better, to understand us better, and being ready and better for the next matches.” On whether Villa can challenge the 'Big 6'... “It depends. We showed it the last years we were, but this year, until now, not. “Of course, other teams, they are not being consistent, they are not being in front of us yet, like Tottenham and Manchester United. “So, we must focus our own way, and of course, our objective is clear: try to be in front of those contenders still to be in the top six, and adding as well there, Newcastle. “But there are other teams every year, not as a surprise, because every year they are as well performing very well, like Brighton, like Bournemouth, like Nottingham Forest – not exactly this year, but they were being fantastic as well – Brentford. “I think the Premier League is very, very difficult because there are a lot of teams, not in the contender positions at the beginning of the season to be in the top positions, but every year, they are always fighting with the teams who should be there. “We are one of the teams, and last year, we achieved it. So, this is the target. This is, as well, the process. We want to try to get consistency, but each year is a test. “And now, in the day nine, we are going to play tomorrow. Our test is Fulham, because they have 8 points, we have 11 points. “Fulham as well, the last year, they were being consistent in the in the table, in the medium positions, but always fighting to be close with the top seven, top six teams.” On Taylor Harwood-Bellis... “Very good. Taylor is a fantastic guy, very professional. He knows how he has to progress with us, understanding everything every day, practising, then playing matches like he’s playing – friendly matches, or two matches in Carabao Cup, Coventry and on Wednesday against Bournemouth, he played a good match. “I like how he is focusing his progression and practising every day, because he knows now, he has to prioritise practising every day to show his progress, and he is doing it.” Click below now to watch Emery's full pre-match press conference via VillaTV...
